prompts.title: Target role shortlist
prompts.use: Turn a vague job hunt into a ranked list.
prompts.text: Act as a career strategist. I work in [current field] and want to move into [target field] in [city or remote]. My strengths are [strengths]. List 8 realistic bridge roles, rank them by fit, and for each one name the single strongest proof point I should build in the next 30 days.

prompts.title: Cold outreach that gets replies
prompts.use: Message a hiring manager without sounding generic.
prompts.text: Write a 90 word LinkedIn message to a hiring manager at [company] for the [role] opening. Reference one specific thing about their product. State what I bring in one sentence. End with a low pressure question. No flattery, no buzzwords.

prompts.title: Referral request to an alum
prompts.use: Ask for a referral without making it awkward.
prompts.text: Draft a short message to a university alum at [company] asking about the [role]. Include why I am a fit in two concrete lines, attach nothing, and make saying no easy. Keep it under 110 words.

prompts.title: Bullet rewrite with impact
prompts.use: Turn a duty into an achievement.
prompts.text: Rewrite this resume bullet using the pattern action verb, what I did, measurable result. Keep it under 22 words and ATS friendly. If a number is missing, give me a placeholder in brackets. Bullet: [paste bullet]

prompts.title: Project to resume bullet
prompts.text: Convert this academic project into two resume bullets for a [role] application. Emphasise tools, scope, and outcome. Do not invent metrics. Project details: [paste details]

prompts.title: Gap and keyword audit
prompts.use: Compare your resume to a job post.
prompts.text: Compare my resume to this job description. List the 12 most important keywords in the posting, mark which appear in my resume, and rewrite my summary to include the top 5 missing ones naturally. Job description: [paste]. Resume: [paste]

prompts.title: STAR answer builder
prompts.use: Structure a story before you tell it.
prompts.text: Turn these rough notes into a STAR answer for the question [question]. Situation in one sentence, task in one sentence, action in three steps, result with a number if I have one. Then give me a 20 second version. Notes: [paste]

prompts.title: Mock interview, one question at a time
prompts.text: Act as a strict but fair interviewer for a [role] role at a [company type] company. Ask one question at a time. After each answer, score it out of 10 on structure, evidence, and clarity. Give one fix. Start with the question a real interviewer would open with.

prompts.title: Weakness answer without a cliche
prompts.text: Help me answer what is your greatest weakness for a [role] interview. Use a real weakness I can defend: [weakness]. Show the concrete system I use to manage it. Under 90 words, no humble brag phrasing.

prompts.title: Headline that ranks and reads well
prompts.use: Fix the line recruiters see first.
prompts.text: Write 5 LinkedIn headlines for a [role] candidate with skills in [skills]. Each must be under 120 characters, include one searchable keyword, and avoid the words passionate, aspiring, and enthusiast.

prompts.title: About section rewrite
prompts.use: Replace a biography with a pitch.
prompts.text: Rewrite my LinkedIn About section in first person, 120 words max. Open with what I do and for whom, give two proof points, close with what I am looking for. No adjectives without evidence. Current text: [paste]

prompts.title: Two career paths, compared
prompts.use: Decide between options with a framework.
prompts.text: Compare a career in [path A] and [path B] for someone with my background: [background]. Use a table with day to day work, entry requirements, salary trajectory in Pakistan, and risk of automation. End with the three questions I should ask myself.

prompts.title: 90 day plan for a new job
prompts.text: Build a 90 day plan for a new [role] at a [company size] company. Split into days 1 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90. For each phase give three actions, one relationship to build, and one thing to avoid.

prompts.title: Explain a career gap
prompts.text: Write a 60 word answer explaining a [length] career gap caused by [reason]. Be direct, take one useful thing from the period, and pivot to why I am ready now. No apology spiral.
